invented.quote: That's more than one in five people at our counters.
invented.why: The brief states that plan members account for about 22 percent of prescriptions filled, not more than one in five people visiting the counters.

invented.quote: Some are teachers and state troopers, others are office staff and retirees.
invented.why: Neither the brief nor the user's additional information mentions the specific occupations or retiree status of the plan members using these pharmacies.

invented.quote: at your current rates we're losing money every time we do.
invented.why: The brief only states that pharmacies lose an average of $1.80 per prescription on the 20 most-filled generic drugs, and the user noted that some pharmacies make up part of the loss on brand-name drugs, not that they lose money every time they serve a member.

invented.quote: That's the gap between what we pay our wholesalers and what the plan's pharmacy benefit manager pays us.
invented.why: The brief does not mention wholesalers and defines the $1.80 loss as the gap between the plan's payment and the combined cost to buy and fill the drug, not just the purchase price.
